Tag: Allow spaces, ignore case and cap at 5
commitResults.messageBody:
Tags must be a single alphanumeric word and are compared
case-sensitively, so "Resident Fellow" cannot be a tag and "RA" and
"ra" are treated as different tags. A contact can have any number of
tags, and they are shown alphabetically rather than in the order they
were added.

RAs categorize contacts with multi-word labels, and a card cluttered
with duplicate or excess tags is slower to scan during an incident.

Let's
* allow letters, digits, spaces and hyphens, up to 50 characters, and
  collapse extra spaces
* compare tags ignoring case and display them with the first letter
  of each word capitalized, keeping acronyms such as "RA" intact
* limit each contact to 5 tags, in add, edit and the data file
* report a specific error for an empty, too long or invalid tag
* keep tags in insertion order on the contact card

The rules live in Tag, Person and ParserUtil so that add, edit and the
upcoming tag command share one definition of a valid tag.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command to tag a contact by name
commitResults.messageBody:
There is no way to add a single tag to an existing contact. The only
option is edit, which needs the contact's index and replaces all of
their tags.

An RA on duty wants to categorize a contact quickly, without first
looking up their index or retyping their existing tags.

Let's add "CONTACT_NAME /tag TAG", which adds one tag to the contact
with that full name, ignoring case and extra spaces. It reports an
error if the contact is not found, already has the tag or has reached
the 5-tag limit.

The input has no command word, so AddressBookParser only treats it as
a tag command when the first word is not a known command word. This
keeps every existing command working as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag command: Tidy code, tests and docs
commitResults.messageBody:
A review of the tag command against the project's code quality, style
and testing guidelines finds a few gaps. The parser and StringUtil use
unnamed string literals, a wrapped lambda is indented 4 spaces instead
of 8, and tests repeat the same tag setup in several classes. The UG
section is much longer than other commands', and the DG lacks a
diagram for the feature.

Let's
* name the regex group and whitespace literals
* fix the wrapped lambda indent in AddressBookParserTest
* share the max-length tags and a 4-tag contact as test fixtures, and
  test a very long contact name
* trim the UG section and the DG manual tests to the essentials, and
  note that the tag command's parameters cannot be reordered
* add a sequence diagram for the tag command to the DG

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tag filter to list command
commitResults.messageBody:
The list command always shows every contact and ignores any text after
it, so there is no way to see only the contacts with a given tag.

An RA on duty often needs one group at a glance, such as all residents
or all hall staff, rather than scanning the full list.

Let's add "list /filter TAG", which shows only contacts with that tag,
ignoring case and extra spaces. Any value is a valid filter; one that
no contact has shows an empty list with a message instead of an error.

Any other text after list is now rejected, so a mistyped filter such
as "list /filtr RA" fails instead of silently showing everyone.

The /filter parsing lives in TagFilterParser so that other output
commands, such as find, can support it by calling the same method.
